method: Seed 128, 512 and 1,024 one-key Durable Objects at in-flight 128, dispose the Miniflare runtime, reopen the same persistent SQLite state in a fresh runtime, then issue one read per key at in-flight 128. Trial two adds a reconstructible latest-value Map to the DO; both trials have exact sequence/revision checks and zero application retries.
interpretation: The per-key actor's warm one-wave profile was fast, but after runtime/actor restart the p99 exceeded 100 ms at all measured key counts. Reconstructing an in-memory latest projection did not solve the cold-activation spike. This motivated the bucketed actor prototype, which trades actors per key for bounded groups of keys per Durable Object.
limitations: Miniflare runtime restart simulates actor reconstruction, not Cloudflare deployment or platform cold-start latency.
No failure injection, sustained offered load, geographically distributed clients or hosted evidence.
Per-key transactions only; no graph-wide transaction or query semantics.
